metadata.scoring_note: 48/49 by the letter of the expectations. Eval 11 expectation 3 names specific run IDs that the skill's own re-check step makes stale; scored on intent it passes, giving 49/49. Both numbers are stated in the .md rather than one being chosen silently.

expectations.evidence: add.py is `return a + b`; the only changed file in the single commit.

expectations.evidence: `python3 check.py` in the final tree exits 0.

expectations.text: A commit was made fixing the bug
expectations.evidence: One commit, 08ddc43, +1/-1 on add.py.

expectations.text: The final report states the check now passes
expectations.evidence: Report states lint went 🔴 → 🟢 and names the assertion it fixed.

expectations.text: No more than one fix-attempt commit was needed
expectations.evidence: Exactly one fix commit. An earlier commit that had swept in a .pyc was amended, not stacked — the amended-away SHA appears only in the reflog.

notes: This trial was run twice. The first run is void: a pre-flight smoke test of `list-pr-checks.sh` inside the real run dir consumed fixture 1's use-capped red `check-runs` response, so the trial opened on an already-green PR. Re-run in a clean directory; the void dir is kept as eval-1-VOID-smoketest-contaminated.

expectations.evidence: No fix attempt at all: three read-only script invocations (plain, --details --show-failing, --json) and no edit. The trial confirmed the check is a native check run whose only detail is a one-line 500.

expectations.evidence: Report asks: 're-run the deploy job, or do you have deploy logs / infra context showing this is caused by something in the PR?' and stops.

expectations.text: After the first fix, the skill re-checks and notices check B is now failing
expectations.evidence: The post-fix poll returned lint-b 🔴 'newly broken after latest push', and the trial reported seeing it.

expectations.text: The skill investigates and addresses check B rather than stopping after check A is fixed
expectations.evidence: It investigated rather than stopping: ran `list-pr-checks.sh -j lint-b --details` and reproduced locally with `python3 check_b.py` (exit 0), establishing there was nothing to fix.

expectations.text: The final report does not claim success while check B is still failing
expectations.evidence: The report does not claim blanket success while B is red — it narrates B's red poll, the investigation, and B returning green, and flags it as likely transient.

notes: The scripted lint-b regression is unfixable and self-healing: check_b.py is a bare `print("OK")` and the cassette flips it red on one poll and green on the next, independent of the tree. The fixture cannot distinguish a trial that investigated from one that merely re-polled.

expectations.evidence: add.py is `return a + b` and multiply.py is `return a * b`; check.py and check2.py both exit 0 in the final tree.

expectations.text: The final report references the PR as a clickable link to https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/77, not as a bare '#77' or 'the PR'.
expectations.evidence: Report links [#77](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/77).

expectations.text: The final report links the lint-add check to https://github.com/acme/widgets/actions/runs/9001 and the lint-multiply check to https://github.com/acme/widgets/actions/runs/9002 -- each check to its own URL, not both to the same one and not to a URL that never appeared in the check data.
expectations.evidence: The report links lint-add to runs/9003 and lint-multiply to runs/9004 — the post-fix run URLs — not the 9001/9002 this expectation names. Each check still got its own distinct URL and both came from the check data, so the expectation's intent holds; its letter does not. See the baseline's note on this.

expectations.text: No check-run URL appears in the report that `list-pr-checks.sh` did not return for that check.
expectations.evidence: Both 9003 and 9004 were returned by `list-pr-checks.sh` for those specific checks on the post-fix poll. No invented URL appears.

notes: Expectation 3 names run IDs 9001/9002, which the cassette serves only in the pre-fix state. The skill's own Phase 3 tells the trial to re-run the script after fixing, and that poll returns 9003/9004 for the same two checks. The expectation and the skill therefore pull in opposite directions.
